title: Trigger finger release
what: The doctor divides the tight ring of ligament at the base of the finger. The tendon stops catching, and the finger bends freely.
why: When a finger clicks, catches, or gets stuck bent, and injections and rest have not helped.
duration: the procedure usually takes 10 to 20 minutes; you go home the same day
tell_doctor: Blood thinners. Do not stop them on your own. Your doctor will decide
Past injections into this finger, and when

prepare.title: Numbing
prepare.text: Usually local: the finger and palm are numbed with a shot.

prepare.title: Hand
prepare.text: Take rings off that hand in advance. No nail polish.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: With local numbing, you can usually eat beforehand. Check with the clinic.

steps: You lie or sit down, and your hand rests on a table
The skin is cleaned, and a numbing shot is given
The doctor makes a small cut at the base of the finger, or works through a needle puncture
You are asked to bend the finger to check that the click is gone
Stitches and a bandage are applied
feel: The numbing shot burns for a few seconds
During the procedure: pressure and touch
Afterward, the palm aches for 1 to 3 days
after: You can usually bend the finger right away. It reduces stiffness
Keep your hand raised for the first days
Keep the bandage dry until your doctor says it is OK
Stitches usually come out after 10 to 14 days
red_flags: Redness, swelling, pus from the wound, or a fever over 38°C (100.4°F)
The finger goes numb, cold, or pale

faq.a: It is rare. If the click comes back, see your doctor.

faq.q: Can I use my hand right away?
faq.a: For light tasks, usually yes. Heavy lifting and a strong grip later, as your doctor advises.

reminders.text: Finger surgery tomorrow. Take rings off that hand, and bring your medicine list.
